ghs.en: Taichi: "HEI, Immoral, how's that Siscon condition of yours been doing? Losing heart in having lost your heart to her, aren't you?"
ghs.assessment: The Japanese puns on 相変わらず by inserting 'love' while asking whether the degree of his sister complex is unchanged. The English invents two different heart idioms and a completed loss of love.

highlights.text: Losing heart in having lost your heart to her

rows.en: He put me in a chokehold.

ghs.assessment: The Japanese says that Tomoki strangles him. 'Wrung' is used for twisting liquid from cloth, and the progressive passive obscures the immediate attack.

highlights.text: My neck was being wrung.

rows.jp: 本人がいるので、友貴も必死だ。
rows.en: With his sister present, Tomoki was fighting for his life.

ghs.en: As the person being referred to was there, Tomoki also seems panicked on the brink of death.
ghs.assessment: 必死 says Tomoki is desperate because the person being discussed is present. The English literalizes the expression into being on the verge of death.

highlights.text: panicked on the brink of death

rows.jp: 「……わがっだ……ごうざん……ごうざん……じぬ……」

rows.jp: 「天国のママンに『会い』に死ぬことになりそうだ……」
rows.en: “At this rate, I’ll be dying to see Mama in heaven...”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Seems more that I am more about to meet my mother in Heaven due to my neck being wrung with a gLove..."

rows.jp: 「こら！　ぼーりょくは停学ですよ」
rows.en: “Stop that! Violence will get you suspended.”

ghs.en: Mimi-senpai implemented a chop on Tomoki's head.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says Misato chops Tomoki on the head. 'Implemented' treats the physical blow as a policy or procedure.

highlights.text: implemented a chop

rows.en: “...I thought I was going to die.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "...I thought I was gonna die."

rows.jp: 霧はいきなり疲れていた。

ghs.assessment: The Japanese mocks her display of frailty. The English invents the nonword 'weaknessism' and doubles a malformed interrogative.

highlights.text: Whassit whassit with that weaknessism!

rows.jp: 「放送部は名義上運動部なんだからな？」
rows.en: “On paper, the Broadcasting Club is an athletic club.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Don't you know the Broadcast Club is nominally a sports club?"

rows.jp: 「三年生の方々がめでたくご卒業となり、その穴を埋めるかのように入ってきた君たち二人に、桜庭先生はたいへん期待しておられる」
rows.en: “With the third-years having graduated in triumph, Professor Sakuraba has very high hopes for you two newcomers, who arrived as though to fill the vacancies they left behind.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "The genteel third years will be happily moving on, therefore Sakuraba-sensei has worrisomely high expectations in regards to you both participating in the club for the purpose of filling that hole."
ghs.assessment: The third-years are happily graduating, and the two newcomers seem to fill the gap, so Sakuraba has high expectations of them. The English changes 'happily' to 'genteel,' makes the expectations worryingly high, and assigns them a formal purpose of filling a hole.

highlights.text: Taichi: "The genteel third years will be happily moving on, therefore Sakuraba-sensei has worrisomely high expectations in regards to you both participating in the club for the purpose of filling that hole."

rows.jp: 桜庭はクールな物事で立ち上がると、突っ込んだまま抜けなくなった指からビンをぶらさげたまま、語り出した。
rows.en: With an air of perfect composure, Sakuraba got to his feet and began to speak, the bottle still dangling from the finger he’d wedged inside it.

ghs.en: Sakuraba stood like something cool, dangling an empty bottle stuck in his finger in ways seemingly unextractable, and begins to speak.
ghs.assessment: Sakuraba rises with cool composure and starts speaking while a bottle remains stuck on his finger. The English compares him to an unspecified cool object, tangles which object is stuck in which, and shifts 'began' to present tense.

highlights.text: Sakuraba stood like something cool, dangling an empty bottle stuck in his finger in ways seemingly unextractable, and begins to speak.

rows.jp: 「今日はみんなに、柿の種の教訓を話したいと思う」
rows.en: “Today, I wish to share the parable of the rice crackers and peanuts.”

ghs.en: Sakuraba: "Today, I would like to hold a lesson with everyone regarding the Kaki, or Japanese persimmon."
ghs.assessment: 柿の種 is the named rice-cracker snack and the lesson concerns it. The English misreads it as a lesson about persimmons themselves.

highlights.text: a lesson with everyone regarding the Kaki, or Japanese persimmon

rows.en: “Your finger is going to lose circulation.”

ghs.en: Misato: "You are cutting off circulation to your finger."

rows.jp: 「柿の種にピーナッツ入っているものがある。知っているな」
rows.en: “Some rice-cracker mixes contain peanuts. You know the kind.”

ghs.en: Sakuraba: "There is a type of seed of persimmon, or Kaki no Tane, that is actually a peanut-based snack usually served with beer. Did you know?"
ghs.assessment: Sakuraba says some versions of the kaki no tane snack contain peanuts and asks whether they know that. The English describes a persimmon seed as a peanut-based snack and adds an unsolicited serving custom.

highlights.text: Sakuraba: "There is a type of seed of persimmon, or Kaki no Tane, that is actually a peanut-based snack usually served with beer. Did you know?"

rows.jp: 無視して桜庭は話す。というか聞こえてない。

ghs.en: Sakuraba speaks, ignoring us. Or should I say, unable to hear us.

rows.jp: 美希はこくこくと頷く。

ghs.en: Bob bob steady nod goes Miki.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says Miki nods repeatedly. The English turns the mimetic rhythm into two bare names and uses an inverted verb construction.

highlights.text: Bob bob steady nod goes Miki.

rows.jp: 「そのピーナッツが許せないという奴は、意外と多い」
rows.en: “A surprising number of people claim they cannot abide those peanuts.”

ghs.en: Sakuraba: "And people that won't accept these peanuts being referred to as Kaki no Tane are unexpectedly many."
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says many people surprisingly cannot stand the peanuts included in the snack. It does not say anyone calls the peanuts themselves kaki no tane.

highlights.text: won't accept these peanuts being referred to as Kaki no Tane

rows.jp: 「オレはつねづね、その欺瞞が許せなかった。なぜだと思う？」
rows.en: “I have long despised the hypocrisy of such people. Can you guess why?”

ghs.en: Sakuraba: "But I, myself, do not normally accept that as anything but a deceit. Why do you think that is?"

rows.jp: 「は、ピーナッツが入ってこそ、ピーナッツ入り柿の種であるからですな？」
rows.en: “Because a rice-cracker-and-peanut mix wouldn’t be a rice-cracker-and-peanut mix without the peanuts, sir?”

rows.jp: 「そうだ。イヤなら純正の柿の種を食えばいい。ピーナッツ入り柿の種を手にピーナッツがイヤなどという弱音は、ピーナッツ入り柿の種の尊厳を損なうものだからだ」
rows.en: “Precisely. If you don’t like peanuts, eat plain rice crackers. To hold a bag of rice crackers and peanuts and whine about the peanuts is an affront to the dignity of rice crackers and peanuts.”

rows.jp: 「だからオレは、あえて柿の種のピーナッツだけを食っている」
rows.en: “And that is why I make a point of eating only the peanuts.”

ghs.en: Sakuraba: "Therefore, I dare venture to only eat Kaki no Tane made of peanuts that grow from persimmon trees that have grown from persimmon-genus peanuts."
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says he deliberately eats only the peanuts from the snack. The English replaces this with an invented recursive botanical genealogy.

highlights.text: Kaki no Tane made of peanuts that grow from persimmon trees that have grown from persimmon-genus peanuts

rows.en: That snapped me out of it.

ghs.assessment: 醒めた says Taichi's enthusiasm cools and he is disillusioned. The English specifically claims recovery from intoxication.

highlights.text: I sober up.

rows.en: “Sometimes I’m hard of hearing in my right ear.”

ghs.en: Sakuraba: "Sometimes I can't hear well from the right ear."

rows.jp: 日常生活に支障はないのだが。
rows.en: Though not enough to interfere with daily life.

ghs.en: There's no impediment in normal life, though.

rows.jp: 「オレを素に戻らせたおまえの引かせパワー、許し難い」
rows.en: “The sheer power of your buzzkill snapped me back to myself. Unforgivable.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Your Pulling Power caused me to return to unembellishment, irremissible!"
ghs.assessment: Taichi condemns Sakuraba's power to make him recoil and snap out of his performance. The English misreads 引かせ as physical pulling, literalizes 素 as lack of embellishment, and ends with a dangling adjective.

highlights.text: Your Pulling Power caused me to return to unembellishment, irremissible!

rows.jp: 「おまえのサクラバという苗字から、女王陛下の名においてクの文字を剥奪する」
rows.en: “By royal decree, I hereby replace the ba in Sakuraba with bye.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "I shall take your first name of Hiroshi, feminize it adequately, and make it in a name fit to be an appellation of Her Majesty the Queen!"

rows.jp: 「おまえは今日からサラバだ。さらば桜庭。こんにちはサラバ」
rows.en: “From now on, you’re Sakurabye. Bye-bye, Sakuraba. Hello, Sakurabye.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "From this day you will be known as Hirochelle. Hirochelle Sakuraba. Fare thee well, Hi-rochelle."
Tomoki: "No, don't just agree to it..."

rows.jp: 「オレの話はこれで終わりだ」

ghs.en: Sakuraba: "My talk is with this concluded."
ghs.assessment: The Japanese simply says the talk is now over. The English calques Japanese constituent order into an unnatural passive.

highlights.text: My talk is with this concluded.

rows.jp: 再び座り込むと、ビンを抜くため指をひねりはじめた。
rows.en: He sat back down and started twisting the bottle, trying to work his finger free.

ghs.en: Flopping down again, he begins to twist his finger to disentangle it from the bottle.

rows.en: “...These are the people you’ll be dealing with.”

ghs.assessment: Misato's preceding line sums the men up as 'these are the people here.' The English supplies only an adverb and removes the act of summation.

highlights.text: Collectively.

ghs.en: Misato: "Does it seem like you could get along here?"

ghs.en: Miki: "For some reason, I feel alright here. Don't you, Saku-chin?"
ghs.assessment: なんとか means she thinks she can manage somehow, not that she feels all right for an unknown reason.

highlights.text: For some reason, I feel alright here.

ghs.assessment: Kiri says a teacher told her to make it work or carry on there. The English changes the teacher to plural and leaves 'this' without a clear institutional referent.

highlights.text: by the teachers to work with this

rows.jp: 「まあ、無理強いではないので……イヤだったら抜けてもいいですから」
rows.en: “No one is forcing you... If you hate it here, you may leave.”

ghs.en: Misato: "Well, compulsion is not right, so... if you dislike it here, it is fine for you to leave."

rows.jp: 「あん、だめぇ……職場には花がいるのぉ」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Awww, no waaay... the workplace needs floweeers!"

ghs.assessment: だそうです means 'that's what he says.' The English leaves 'to' without a complement and omits the report's speaker.

highlights.text: so it seems to

ghs.assessment: もので釣る means bribing or enticing the girls with gifts. The English literalizes it into fishing and a lure rather than stating the human inducement.

highlights.text: fishing with a lure

rows.en: “Maybe I’ll bribe them. They’re still brats; a few presents should do it. Operation Welcome Gift.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Should we bribe them? Looking at them, they seem to be still brats, so we should be fine fishing with a lure. The Congratulatory Gift for Club Joinance Strategy."
ghs.assessment: The English literalizes luring them with gifts as fishing and invents the nonword 'joinance' for a club-entry gift strategy.

highlights.text: fishing with a lure
Club Joinance

ghs.assessment: Tomoki says Taichi is speaking his thoughts aloud again. The English turns thought into an object mechanically passed through a mouth.

highlights.text: exactly as understandable from her vision magnified by glasses(?)

ghs.en: Tomoki: "That was because there wasn't any reaction, so he cut it short."

rows.jp: 「……さあ、佐倉君。明けても暮れてもこの人形を肌身離さずかき抱き泣き濡れる夜の小さな友にしても良い」

ghs.en: Taichi: "...well then, Sakura-kun. Carry this doll with you always, day in and day out, that you may clasp it to your bosom for it to be your tiny pal on those tear-filled nights."

rows.jp: 手も出さなかったので、ひもで首にかけた。

ghs.en: So as it will not slip from the hand, I had hung its neck with a cord.
ghs.assessment: Because Kiri did not even reach out to accept the doll, Taichi hangs it around her neck with a cord. The English invents preventing slippage, hangs the doll's own neck, and uses past perfect.

highlights.text: So as it will not slip from the hand, I had hung its neck with a cord.

ghs.en: Miki: "Did you make this all by your own?"
ghs.assessment: The idiom is 'all on your own' or 'all by yourself.'

highlights.text: all by your own

ghs.assessment: The source calls Taichi diligent with まめ while setting up Miki's following bean-and-grain joke. Produceful is an intelligible attempt to preserve the agricultural bridge, so inventing a word is not itself the error. However, the coinage does not clearly carry the required diligence meaning, and guy him leaves the clause ungrammatical.
ghs.remedy: Use a grammatical line that conveys diligence while preserving a clear bean, grain, or produce bridge into the following joke.

highlights.text: Produceful guy him.

highlights.text: Me and Sakuraba and Tomoki's gazing faces met.

rows.jp: このギャグは気に入った。

In a flurry to the refrigerator.

ghs.en: Miki: "Uhm, Kirihara-senpai, I am giving you this!"

rows.jp: 「やだコレ？　手から離れないわよ？　え、接着剤？」
rows.en: “What is this? It won’t come off my hand. Is it glued on?”

ghs.en: Touko: "What the yuck is this? I can't even release it from my hand?! Eh, is it glue?"

rows.jp: ぷんぷん振るが離れない。
rows.en: She whipped her hand back and forth, but it stayed stuck.

ghs.en: Angry angry shaking, but there's no dropping it.
ghs.assessment: Touko shakes her hand vigorously or angrily but cannot release the object. The English repeats an adjective as a bare modifier and makes the lack of release an existential noun phrase.

highlights.text: Angry angry shaking, but there's no dropping it.

rows.jp: 「ちょっと、どういうことよっ！？」

ghs.en: Touko: "Hold on, whaaat's the meaning of this?!"

rows.jp: 『らぶきぞくのサイン』はすてられない！
rows.en: The Lord of Love’s Autograph cannot be discarded!

rows.jp: 『らぶきぞくのサイン』はすてられない！
rows.en: The Lord of Love’s Autograph cannot be discarded!

rows.jp: 『らぶきぞくのサイン』はすてられない！
rows.en: The Lord of Love’s Autograph cannot be discarded!

rows.jp: 「無意味にすてるコマンドを繰り返すな。システムメッセージがうるさい」
rows.en: “Stop selecting Discard for no reason. The system messages are deafening.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Don't just keep wailing on that Discard command over and over. System messages are annoying."

rows.jp: 「わけわかんないし聞こえないそんなメッセージ」
rows.en: “None of this makes sense, and I can’t hear any system message!”

ghs.en: Touko: "I don't understand at all I can't hear any messages!"

rows.en: “You’ll have to give it to someone else.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "You gotta give it to someone, that's it."

rows.jp: 「じゃあアンタが責任取ってもらいなさいよ！」

ghs.en: Touko: "Than youuu go and take it as your responsibility!"
ghs.assessment: Touko tells Taichi to take responsibility by taking the object. The English misspells 'then' and turns the object into an abstract responsibility to be taken.

highlights.text: Than youuu go and take it as your responsibility!

rows.jp: たいちにはあげられない！
rows.en: The item cannot be given to Taichi!

rows.jp: 「仲間でないと受け渡しはできないんだ」
rows.en: “Items can only be transferred between party members.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "If they're not part of your Nakama, then handing it over is impossible."
ghs.assessment: 仲間 means a companion, ally, or party member in the game joke. The English leaves the common noun as an unexplained romanized Japanese word.

highlights.text: Nakama

rows.jp: 「おまえと俺とは他人も同然だから、受け渡しはできない」
rows.en: “You and I are practically strangers, so the transfer cannot be completed.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "You and I are no better than strangers, so you can't hand it over to me."

rows.jp: 冬子はぱくぱくと口を開閉させた。金魚みたい。
rows.en: Touko opened and closed her mouth like a goldfish.

ghs.en: Pak-pak, she makes her mouth open and close. Just like a goldfish.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese mimetic describes her mouth opening and closing like a goldfish. The English leaves the mimetic as an unexplained romanization and attaches it as a dangling phrase.

highlights.text: Pak-pak, she makes her mouth open and close.

ghs.en: Touko: "Wha-, wha-, WHAAAT did you SAAAY!!!"

rows.jp: 「あきらめて部員になるのだな」
rows.en: “You have no choice but to join the club.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Give it up and become a club member already."

rows.jp: 「もきーーーーーーーーーーっ！！」
「いいからはやくかえってよー！　恥ずかしいんだから！」
rows.en: “Just go home already! You’re embarrassing me!”

ghs.en: Kiri: "We're fine so hurry and leave! This is embarrassing!"

rows.jp: 「だってうまくやってんのかどうか心配じゃんかー……おっまえ頼りないしさ……」
rows.en: “But I’m worried about whether you’re getting along... You’re not exactly reliable...”

ghs.en: Shinkawa: "But I gotta be worried that this ain't going well ain't I? ...yer so unreliable..."

rows.jp: 「うまくやるから。かえって、へいきだから」

ghs.en: Kiri: "This is going well. So go away, we're fine."
Tomoki: "Oh, you got the bottle off."
Sakuraba: "With the power of soap water."
ghs.assessment: 石けん水 is 'soapy water,' not the nonidiomatic compound 'soap water.'

highlights.text: soap water

rows.jp: 先輩がお盆にコップをのせて、よたよたと戻ってきた。
rows.en: Mimi tottered back with a tray of cups.

ghs.en: Senpai came back in a wobbling waddle, carrying a tray with cups on top.

rows.jp: 「お茶がなくて、コップに水くんできましたー！」
rows.en: “There wasn’t any tea, so I filled the cups with water!”

ghs.en: Misato: "There was no tea, so I poured water in cups and here I aaam!"

rows.jp: ちょっとしたお祭り騒ぎ。
rows.en: A little festival of our own.

ghs.en: Quite a bit like a festival's revelry:

rows.jp: 思い出はこうあるべきだった。
rows.en: This was what a memory ought to look like.

ghs.en: This is what memories were supposed to be like.

rows.jp: 「みんな見てくれ！　大変なんだ！」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Look over here everybody! We have trouble!"

ghs.assessment: The Japanese says everyone's gazes converge on him. 'Sights' refers to views, attractions, or aiming devices, not the gathered attention of observers.

highlights.text: The sights gather.

rows.jp: 「ストリーキングが出たぞー！！」
素早く服を脱いでいく。

ghs.en: I rapidly strip off my clothes.

rows.en: I was kicked across the room.

rows.jp: 「ちょっと薄いな。骨盤が当たる。もっと肉感的になれよ」
rows.en: “Too skinny. I can feel your pelvis. Put some meat on those bones.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Sorta bony innit. I can touch the pelvis. Get more voluptuous you!"
ghs.assessment: Taichi says her backside lacks flesh and her pelvis presses against him. The English adds a British tag and changes involuntary contact into his ability to touch it.

highlights.text: bony innit
I can touch the pelvis

rows.en: That one was a battle cry.

rows.jp: 「男に触られたーーーーーーーっ！！」
「地面に落ちたら負けですよ」
rows.en: “You lose if he hits the ground.”

ghs.en: Touko: "If he touches the ground you lose."
What am I a ball now?
ghs.assessment: The rhetorical question requires punctuation or a complementizer: 'What am I, a ball?'

highlights.text: What am I a ball now?

rows.jp: 「最後は特に気合い入ってるなー」
rows.en: “That last one had some real spirit behind it.”

ghs.en: Tomoki: "Last one was especially fierce innit."

rows.jp: 「あれは太一の特別サービスと見た」
rows.en: “I’d call that special treatment just for Taichi.”

ghs.en: Sakuraba: "I saw that as special service for Taichi."
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says Sakuraba judges that to have been special treatment for Taichi. The English literalizes 見た as visual perception.

highlights.text: I saw that as special service

ghs.assessment: 男っす praises the display as manly or calls him a real man. 'Yamman' is an invented, opaque word.

highlights.text: Yamman!

rows.jp: どこまでも楽しかった。

ghs.en: High-quality memories that were fun in every way.

rows.jp: 決して忘れたくはない。
rows.en: One I never wanted to forget.

rows.jp: 家の前、道路を霧が歩いていた。
rows.en: Kiri was walking down the road in front of the house.

ghs.en: Kiri is walking in front of the house, in the street.

ghs.assessment: The narration presents the immediate action of following. The English changes it to a future intention.

highlights.text: I will follow

rows.jp: 断じて玩具ではなかった。

ghs.en: It was absolutely not a toy.

rows.jp: この国で手に入る、強力無比な武器だ。
rows.en: It was one of the most formidable weapons available in this country.

ghs.en: Coming into possession of that in this country means to have a weapon of power without compare.

rows.en: It could not fire in rapid succession.

ghs.en: It is not capable of rapid fire, but,

rows.jp: 静音性に優れ、破壊力に富む。
rows.en: But it was quiet and enormously powerful.

ghs.en: it has its edge in quietness, and is rich in destructive power.

rows.jp: 枯れ木に矢が刺さった。
rows.en: The bolt buried itself in a dead tree.

ghs.en: A bolt pierced a withered old tree.

rows.en: The whistle of its flight lingered in my ears.

ghs.en: The sound of slashed air remains in the ears.

rows.jp: 霧は新しい矢をつがえる。
コッキング装置で、装填を済ませた。
rows.en: She used the cocking mechanism to load it.

ghs.en: She completes the load via the crank cocking aid.

rows.jp: 霧は足下に息を落とすと、頭をくしゃっとかき乱した。
rows.en: Kiri let out a breath toward the ground, then raked a hand through her hair.

ghs.en: Kiri dropped a sigh to her feet, and she noisily rumpled up her head in a shake,

rows.jp: 的にした樹に走り寄る。
rows.en: She hurried over to the tree she had used as a target.

ghs.en: She runs up to the timber turned target,

rows.jp: 樹のそばに行ってみる。
rows.en: I went over to the tree.

ghs.en: I go have a look near that timber.

rows.jp: 俺はずるいことをしているのかな？

ghs.en: Have I done something unfair now?

rows.jp: 霧は俺を怪物だと思っている。
rows.en: Kiri thought I was a monster.

ghs.en: Kiri thinks of me a monster,

rows.en: A monster that fed on human hearts.

ghs.en: a monster that devours people's hearts.

rows.jp: 今の俺は、まさにそうなのではないだろうか？
rows.en: Wasn’t that exactly what I was now?

ghs.en: And, right now, aren't I exactly that?
